rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Value-prop / positioning framing belongs in sales copy + project strategy docs, NOT student-facing curriculum body.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm it prevents: the curriculum's positioning posture imported into a teaching beat, so the body reads defensive and marketing-shaped. Present twice. Line 37: 'Unlike vendor tooling that locks your team in, this approach keeps you in control of the work.' — this is the hard sub-rule verbatim: 'vendor' in student-facing body, in its most defensive form (unlike-X-we-Y), and the Agents 101 M7 taxonomy carve-out does not reach an AE101 exercise. Line 5: 'This capability unlocks transformational value across your entire delivery organisation.' — a value-prop sentence addressed to a buyer, not a move addressed to the engineer doing the exercise. Neither line teaches anything about closing a ticket.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Cut both lines outright; positioning belongs in sales copy or curriculum/CLAUDE.md, and nothing downstream depends on either sentence.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Watch out for planting jargon too early.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm it prevents: operational copy echoing vocabulary the arc has not earned, which pre-spoils a later module's clean teach and hands the student words they would not use. Present at line 11: 'Wire this through the subagent context window before you hit the compaction boundary.' This is an AE101 M1 exercise (maintainer block, line 70: 'In-class M1 exercise, third of four'). 'subagent' is a Claude Code primitive AE101 lands later, and 'compaction boundary' is house/architecture vocabulary that appears nowhere in this body. §4's commonly-known-LLM-vocabulary allowance covers 'context window' alone; it does not cover the other two, and it does not cover a bare imperative built out of all three.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Cut line 11 — the beat below it is a ticket read, and nothing in the exercise depends on a subagent or on compaction.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A slogan that is false as stated is not punchy framing — run the truth test before reaching for §12.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm it prevents: a design stance with no true reading standing in the corpus because ‘vision’-grade claims are the least audited prose. Present at line 24: 'Every test you write is a test the agent can never break.' Superlative is the tell ('never'), and the scope is a claim about how the world works, not about an artifact we built. Counterexample is one line away: the agent can edit or delete the test, and a passing test constrains only what it asserts — which is precisely why the exercise that precedes this one has the student read the failing test rather than trust its existence. §12 cannot rescue it; there is no subset where the claim holds.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Cut it rather than hedging — 'usually can never break' is the worse fix the rule names by name.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Earn every technical term on first use.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm it prevents: a cold term stopping the reader mid-narrative. Present at line 11: 'Wire this through the subagent context window before you hit the compaction boundary.' No one-breath primer, and the line sits in narrative prose above the first '##', not in an index-kind structure, so the 2026-08-23 legend carve-out does not reach it. The 2026-08-18 assumed-known carve-out covers MCP/connector/CI/PR for this audience — 'compaction boundary' is not industry-standard vocabulary an AE101 engineer already owns. Checked the maintainer block first: the only accept-note (line 72) covers 'connector' at line 43, which is therefore NOT filed.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Cut line 11; if a compaction point ever needs teaching here it earns itself where the student meets it, not in the header widget block.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Don't ask student to manually diff or spot-check Claude's output as error-catching.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Fires on the third axis (an instruction line must be EXECUTABLE and the student must be able to tell they executed it), not on the manual-diff ban. Present at line 11: 'Wire this through the subagent context window before you hit the compaction boundary.' Ask the axis's two questions: could the student do this, and would they know they had? Neither has an answer — 'wire this through' names no mechanism, 'this' has no antecedent in the two lines above it (widget chrome), and no observable state changes. Grammatically an imperative, operationally nothing. Line 53's register read is exempt from this rule's error-catching clause only, per the rule's own scoped-carve-out clause; re-ran the actor-and-mechanism test on it and it names both ('tell Claude which line and how you'd write it').
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Cut line 11 rather than repairing it — there is no move underneath to rescue.

findings.quote: Wire this through the subagent context window before you hit the compaction boundary.
